summary: Edward S. Casey is a philosopher who studied at Yale, Northwestern, and the Sorbonne under Paul Ricœur. He taught at UC Santa Barbara, Yale, and Emory, served as Dean at Stony Brook (~1978), and was APA president (2009–2010).

Edward Said worked in philosophy and literature. He studied at Princeton (~1953–1957) and Harvard (~1957–1964), and taught English and Comparative Literature at Columbia University from around 1963 to 2003.

Linguist Edward Sapir studied at Columbia under Wilhelm Wundt and Franz Boas. He headed the Anthropology Division at the Geological Survey of Canada (~1910–1925) and held posts at the University of Chicago (~1925–1931) and Yale University (~1931–1939).

Edward Upham worked in Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. Between approximately 1824 and 1834, he was a member of the Royal Asiatic Society and a fellow of the Society of Antiquaries of London.

Edward Vernon Arnold was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Cambridge and Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth. He was a fellow at Trinity College, Cambridge (~1880–1886) and professor at Bangor University from 1884 to 1924.

Edward Washburn Hopkins worked in Indology and linguistics. After studies at Columbia and Leipzig under Albrecht Weber and Ernst Windisch, he taught at Columbia (1881–1885), Bryn Mawr (1885–1895), and succeeded William Dwight Whitney at Yale (1895–1926).

Edward Winslow Bastian works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Banaras Hindu University and the University of Wisconsin-Madison, training under Geshe Lhundub Sopa, Geshe Lobsang Tenzin, Geshe Lobsang, and Geshe Lobsang Donyo.

Edwin Arnold was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology who studied at Oxford. He served as Principal of Deccan College (1856), Fellow at the University of Mumbai (~1856–1861), and founded the Maha Bodhi Society.

Edwin F. Bryant is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. After earning his doctorate at Columbia University (~1990–1997), he taught at Harvard University (~1998–2003) and served as Associate Professor of Hinduism at Rutgers University (~2003).

Edwin Felix Thomas Atkinson was an Indologist and historian who studied at Trinity College Dublin (~1857–1861). He served as President of The Asiatic Society (1886–1887) and Accountant General for the Government of Bengal (attested 1889).

Edwin Gerow is an Indologist and philosopher who studied under J. A. B. van Buitenen, Louis Renou, and George V. Bobrinskoy. He held posts at the University of Washington (~1967–1978) and Reed College (~1978–2003).

Edwin Norris was a linguist, historian, and Indologist. He worked at the East India Company (1818–1837) and Foreign Office (1847–1866), while holding long-term posts including secretary and librarian at the Royal Asiatic Society (~1836–1872).

Linguist and Indologist Edwin Whitfield Fay earned his Ph.D. at Johns Hopkins (1886–1890) and studied at Leipzig. He held posts at the University of Michigan, Washington and Lee University (1893–1899), and the University of Texas at Austin.

Egaku Maeda studied Buddhist studies and Indology at the University of Tokyo under Naoshiro Tsuji, Shoson Miyamoto, Hajime Nakamura, and Kogen Mizuno. He held professorships at Tokai Gakuen, Meijo, and Aichi Gakuin University (1972–2002).

Eido Tai Shimano was a Buddhist studies figure who trained under Kengan Goto, Keizan Shirozou, and Soen Nakagawa. He led the Zen Studies Society (~1965–2010), New York Zendo Shobo-ji (~1968–2012), and Dai Bosatsu Zendo Kongo-ji (~1976–2012).

Eiichi Makino was a scholar of philosophy and other fields who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1900–1903). He spent his main academic career teaching at the University of Tokyo (~1903–1938) and Shiraume Gakuen Junior College (~1957–1966).
Eiichi Yamaguchi is an Indologist and philosopher. He completed graduate studies at Kyushu University (attested 1986–1990) and served there as a Research Assistant (attested 1990–1991).

Eiki Hoshino is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who studied at Taisho University (~1962–1966). He served as a Professor in the Faculty of Humanities and Director at Taisho University (~1980–2013).

Historian Eileen Power studied at Girton College, Cambridge (~1907–1910) and the University of Paris (~1910–1911). From around 1921 to 1940, she held posts at the University of London and the London School of Economics.

Eisaku Okada specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Kyoto University (attested 2014) and held posts at the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science, Koyasan University, and Kyoto University (attested 2014–2015).
